newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - June 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - June 23.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.
- The leaders of eight leading countries called on North Korea to stop the "development, deployment and export" of missiles in a joint communique issued at the Denver summit.
- President Kim Young-sam is to arrive in New York on the morning of June 22 on the first leg of his nine-day overseas trip.
- In a landmark settlement, the U.S. tobacco industry Friday accepted tough government regulation of cigrettes and agreed to pay billion of dollars in damages for the health effects of smoking.

- Starting in July, the business barriers separating the nation's banks, securities firms and insurance companies will be nearly eradicated under government efforts to boost the competitiveness of the industry, said the Ministry of Finance and Economy.
- Brokerage houses will be free to set commissions, beginning Sept. 1, when the ceiling on commissions is abolished.
